newsitem.title: USA: Sportscaster Albert to provide dental impression.
newsitem.headline: Sportscaster Albert to provide dental impression.

text.p: NBC sportscaster Marv Albert on Thursday agreed to provide a dental impression sample as part of the criminal case against him alleging that he bit and sexually assaulted a woman, a prosecutor said.

Albert, 53, is charged with forcible sodomy and assault for allegedly forcing a 42-year-old woman to perform oral sex and biting her repeatedly in an Arlington, Va., hotel room in February. Oral sex is regarded as sodomy under Virginia law.

Albert, a veteran basketball and hockey broadcaster best known for his trademark "Yes!" after a good play, faces a sentence of life plus 12 years if convicted on both counts. He vehemently denies the charges.
He was in Arlington County Circuit Court on Thursday as his lawyers and prosecutors brought pre-trial motions before Judge Benjamin Kendrick.

Albert's lawyers agreed to a prosecution request that he provide a dental impression as part of the investigation, said Theo Stamos, a member of the Arlington County prosecuting team. Albert's previous defence lawyer also said the defendant would be willing to provide such an impression.
"It's something that will be done with dental impressions," Stamos said. "He's agreed to return to Arlington (to provide the impression)."
Lawyers for both sides refused to comment on the importance of comparing Albert's dental impression to bite marks on the alleged victim's body.
Stamos said the prosecution and defence also agreed to seal some court documents "to protect people's privacy rights on both sides."
Albert is free pending a promise to pay $1,000 should he fail to appear in court. Trial is set for Sept. 22.

Albert just completed his 30th season as the voice of the New York Knicks professional basketball team and his 32nd season broadcasting for the New York Rangers hockey team. He also covers sporting events for NBC including professional football, boxing and the Olympic Games, and does a humorous bloopers segment on late-night comedy shows.
The alleged assault in Virginia occurred while he was in the Washington area for a New York Knicks-Washington Bullets National Basketball Association game.
